title: Discharge Re-Test Days Near the End of Work Conditioning and Work Hardening
content:
# Discharge re-test days

**Standard.** On an extension of the Work Conditioning Program or the Work Hardening Program under a Workers' Compensation Referral, the discharge re-test days are one (1) where the whole weeks remaining before the program's maximum length do not exceed the request window and a completed functional capacity evaluation is on file, two (2) where they do not exceed the request window and no completed functional capacity evaluation is on file, and none otherwise.

- **Whole weeks remaining** — the program's maximum length in days (its maximum length in weeks multiplied by seven) less the calendar days since the initial evaluation, divided by seven and rounded down; the initial evaluation is the date of service of the referral's evaluation charge. The maximum length is 6 weeks in the Work Conditioning Program and 8 weeks in the Work Hardening Program.
- **Request window** — the whole weeks the extension asks the adjuster to cover.
- **Completed functional capacity evaluation on file** — as shown on the referral record.

## Combinations

| Whole weeks remaining compared with the request window | Completed FCE on file | Discharge re-test days |
|---|---|---|
| equal to or fewer than the window | yes | 1 |
| equal to or fewer than the window | no | 2 |
| more than the window | any | none |

## Cases (hypothetical)

- 2 whole weeks remain and the request window is 2 weeks; a completed FCE is on file: 1 day.
- 1 whole week remains and the window is 1 week; no completed FCE on file: 2 days.
- 4 whole weeks remain and the window is 3 weeks: none.
